newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Botham to shave head for charity.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Botham to shave head for charity.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Feb 14 - English cricketing great and charity worker Ian Botham will shave his head if Evening Post readers donate $50,000 for cancer research.

Botham, in New Zealand helping to coach the England cricket side and commentating for British television, was talked into the dare which follows Kiwi Chris Cairns' promise to shed his locks in Christchurch if $20,000 is given to the Child Cancer Research Foundation.
The shedding of hair is part of a nationwide Crop-A-Cop fund-raiser which has the backing of police and Rotary.
"I'm always keen to do anything I can to help the cause of child cancer research," Botham said.
He will have his head shaved during the one-day international at Wellington's Basin Reserve on March 4 if the $50,000 target is reached.
"Half of me hopes you don't get it, the other half hopes you do.
"My hair will grow again, kids with cancer sometimes don't."
Botham said his wife Kathy had laughed when he told her of his plans.
"We're going to the French Alps for a family skiing holiday when I get back, so I'll be buying a balaclava."
Botham has raised more than $12.4 million during 20 years of commitment to help child cancer victims.
His interest was sparked by the plight of four young sufferers he saw in a hospital ward when he was receiving treatment for an injured foot.
His most famous exploits have been the 1410km John O'Groats to Land's End walk and the retracing of Hannibal's journey 700km over the French Alps with three elephants.
